beats.narration_text: Hola — this is Liam, in for Bear. Kimi K3 just published a table showing it beats almost every AI model. I asked Claude to actually read the footnotes. Here's what came back: thirty-four benchmarks, six models, one table. The headline claim is real — but the fine-grained rankings carry five separate credibility problems. Here's the audit.

beats.narration_text: Act one. The claim.

Table two. Kimi K3 versus Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, and GLM-5.2. Thirty-four benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and tools. The headline: K3 beats all of them — except the top two.

lines: Table 2. K3 vs Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol,

beats.narration_text: Their exact language: 'consistently outperforms other open and proprietary models evaluated in our suite.' Strong claim. Let's see if the table supports it.

production_viz.label: their claim — quote card with emphasis
production_viz.mechanic: cream card; quote text types in: 'consistently outperforms other open and proprietary models evaluated in our suite.' — terracotta highlight ring draws on around 'our suite'; serif EB Garamond, no other decoration
production_viz.note: the caveat phrase 'our suite' is the tell — flag it before revealing the hedge

beats.narration_text: The first hedge is in their own abstract: 'its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models — Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.' So the ceiling is already disclosed. They're telling you where they lose before you find it.
beats.prompt: SHOPPING: Tier 2 — PDF abstract screenshot. Render from k3_tech_report.pdf page 1-2. Rights: Moonshot AI tech report, fair use for citation still. drawon ring on the caveat sentence about trailing Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.

beats.narration_text: Act two. Home field.

First problem: every model in Table 2 runs under a different agent harness. K3 runs on Kimi Code — Moonshot's own harness. GPT models run on Codex. Claude models on Claude Code. These are not equivalent scaffolds.

lines: Each model runs its own harness.

beats.narration_text: A harness is the scaffolding that plans multi-step tasks, writes and executes code, handles retries. The model's score is model times harness. You cannot read one without the other.

production_viz.label: model × harness → benchmark score
production_viz.mechanic: two input boxes on the left: 'MODEL' (teal) and 'HARNESS' (crimson); a multiplication symbol between them; arrow pointing right to 'BENCHMARK SCORE' (slate box); annotation below: 'you cannot read one without the other'
production_viz.note: the equation is the point — establish it before numbers

beats.narration_text: The paper shows the cross-harness gap. On K C B 2.0 internal benchmark: K3 scores 72.9 on Kimi Code, but 73.7 on Claude Code. GPT-5.6 Sol scores only 64.8 on Codex. These gaps are large and uncontrolled.

A ten-point swing from harness choice is plausible on agentic coding benchmarks. The whole-table comparison is not a model quality comparison. It's model-plus-harness versus model-plus-different-harness.
beats.prompt: SHOPPING: Tier 1 — two-terminal or two-IDE conceptual shot, any stock photo of split screens showing different coding environments. No real person. Represents model + harness A vs model + harness B.

beats.narration_text: The honest version: K3 plus Kimi Code performs at this level. Whether K3 plus Claude Code, or K3 plus a neutral harness, matches or exceeds that — this table cannot tell you.

production_viz.label: known vs unknown harness combinations
production_viz.mechanic: left side: 'K3 + Kimi Code' box (teal) with an arrow to a score; right side: 'K3 + ?' box (slate, dashed border) with arrow to large '?' in crimson; label above right: 'this table cannot tell you'; column heads in MONO serif
production_viz.note: the honest version beat — what we know versus what remains unknown

beats.narration_text: Act three. The footnotes.
The two models that beat K3 — Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol — are systematically caveated downward. Look at the table headers: 'with fallback' and 'with cyberguards.'

lines: Models that beat K3 — caveated down.

beats.narration_text: On S W E-Marathon, footnote: Fable 5 hits fallback on 35 percent of tasks. On Agents' Last Exam, Fable 5 runs at x-high with 40 percent of tasks annotated as downgraded. These aren't full-capability runs.

production_viz.label: Fable 5 fallback impact on SWE-Marathon
production_viz.mechanic: two bars side by side: Fable 5 SWE-Marathon 35.0 (crimson, labeled '35% fallback') and K3 42.0 (teal); annotation below Fable 5 bar: 'at full capability, gap likely wider'; gold asterisk on the caveat; MONO score labels
production_viz.note: the fallback annotation is the tell — K3 still loses to this degraded version

beats.narration_text: Here's the tell: K3 still loses to these degraded versions. Which means the real gap to Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol at full capability is larger, not smaller, than the table shows. The footnotes actually invert the usual marketing move.
beats.prompt: Extract from kimi-demo-short.mp4 at t=2s. ffmpeg -ss 2 -i kimi-demo-short.mp4 -frames:v 1 pantry/B14-kimi-hype.png. Credit: Moonshot AI / Kimi K3 promotional video. Vendor hype frame — cut to the 'still loses' finding.

beats.narration_text: Takeaway: if you're scanning to see how far K3 trails the frontier, the table underreports the gap. The caveats narrow it artificially.

production_viz.label: apparent vs real gap to frontier
production_viz.mechanic: horizontal gap diagram: K3 on the left (teal dot), frontier on the right (slate dot); narrow bar labeled 'apparent gap (Table 2)' in crimson; wider annotation bracket labeled 'real gap ≥ apparent gap' in slate; gold line shows caveat shrink arrow
production_viz.note: the punchline of the footnotes act — the table undercounts the gap

beats.narration_text: Act four. Modified benchmarks.

Three headline coding benchmarks are modified from their public versions. S W E-Marathon: an H20-calibrated branch prior to v1.1 release. PostTrainBench: run on H20, not the official H100 config. FrontierSWE: dominance scores recomputed from raw scores.

Each modification is individually defensible — hardware availability is real, standardization takes time. Collectively: K3's three strongest coding results all ride on non-standard variants assembled by the authors.

production_viz.label: three modified benchmarks, compound risk
production_viz.mechanic: three rectangular boxes in a row: 'SWE-Marathon', 'PostTrainBench', 'FrontierSWE'; each has a gold 'modified' tag in the top-right corner; a compound risk arrow arcs over all three labeled 'K3's three strongest coding results — all non-standard'; colors slate box backgrounds, gold tags
production_viz.note: individually defensible, collectively a pattern — that's the point

beats.narration_text: Reproducibility problem: no third party can run the H20-calibrated SWE-Marathon branch. These are results on a benchmark only Moonshot's lab can run. That's not malfeasance — it's just not independently checkable.

out.text: ERROR: benchmark branch is internal to Moonshot AI lab
Reproduction requires access to H20-calibrated task set
This result cannot be independently verified.

beats.prompt: SHOPPING: Tier 1 — terminal/CI output aesthetic, any screenshot of a failed test run or 'benchmark not available' message. No real person. Represents reproducibility failure.

beats.narration_text: Act five. No error bars.
Table 2 reports single point estimates. Zero confidence intervals. Zero standard deviations. No seed counts on most rows. One number per benchmark per model.
GPQA Diamond: GPT-5.6 Sol 94.1, K3 93.5, GPT-5.5 93.5, Fable 5 92.6. A 1.5-point cluster. At typical sampling variance of plus-or-minus 0.5 to 1.0 on these tests, every position is interchangeable.

production_viz.label: GPQA Diamond — four models in a 1.5-point cluster
production_viz.mechanic: bar chart, four bars from 92.0 to 95.0 range: GPT-5.6 Sol 94.1 (slate), K3 93.5 (teal), GPT-5.5 93.5 (slate tint), Fable 5 92.6 (slate); y-axis 91–95; then a second pass overlays ±1.0 error bars on each bar — all bars touch or overlap; annotation: 'every position is interchangeable'
production_viz.note: the error bar overlay is the reveal — show clean bars first, then add uncertainty

beats.narration_text: The prose says K3 is 'just 0.2 points behind' and 'essentially tied.' Without error bars, 0.2 points is not a ranking. It's a number with no interpretable meaning.

beats.act: ACT VI: The Signal Worth Trusting
beats.narration_text: Act six. The signal worth trusting.

lines: ACT VI: The Signal Worth Trusting

beats.narration_text: Three independent evaluators. Artificial Analysis: number four of 580 models, Elo 1547. Vals AI: number two of 39 in the frontier tier. LMArena WebDev Arena: number one open model — first open model ever to top it.

production_viz.label: three independent evaluator placements
production_viz.mechanic: three rows, each an evaluator: 'Artificial Analysis' (teal label) — '#4 / 580 models, Elo 1547'; 'Vals AI' (teal) — '#2 / 39 frontier models'; 'LMArena WebDev Arena' (teal) — '#1 open model — first ever'; K3 position in each row highlighted gold; 'INDEPENDENT' stamp in slate across the top
production_viz.note: three orgs, three methodologies, all converge — that's the corroboration signal

beats.narration_text: These are run without Moonshot's harness. Different methodologies. No shared test setup. All three land K3 at or near the top of the open field, clearly above Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5.
beats.prompt: SHOPPING: Tier 1 — AI benchmark leaderboard screenshot aesthetic, any publicly available model ranking site. No real person required. Represents independent third-party ranking convergence.

beats.narration_text: Simon Willison, an independent developer, published his own tests. His framing: 'mostly beating Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 while losing to Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.' That's the defensible landing zone. Not the Table 2 decimals.
beats.prompt: SHOPPING: Tier 2 — Simon Willison blog post screenshot (simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/16/kimi-k3/). Public blog post, citation use. drawon ring on key sentence: 'mostly beating Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 while losing to Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.'

beats.narration_text: The narrow defensible claim: best open-weight model as of July 2026, competitive with second-tier proprietary models, clearly behind the top two. Every independent evaluator supports this. The fine-grained Table 2 wins do not.

Kimi K3 is real — the best open model in the world right now, and that's corroborated by three independent evaluators who ran it without Moonshot's scaffolding. But the specific Table 2 rankings carry home-harness advantage, systematically degraded competitors, author-modified benchmarks, and no error bars. Trust the coarse direction. Treat every decimal in Table 2 as noise.

Your turn. Pick a task where you know the right answer — not a benchmark, a real problem. Run it on K3 and on Opus 4.8 back to back. Same prompt, same context. You're doing what this paper couldn't: one fixed test, no harness asymmetry, no footnotes.
